the pathogenesis of vascular lesions in hypertension.
the role of ET-1 in the development of hypertensive vascular injury.
the potential role of ET-1 in the production of vascular lesions.

ET-1 is not the only mediator involved in the pathogenesis and development of vascular damage.
the present data indicate a potential role of endothelin in the pathogenesis and/or progression of acute vascular disease.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ET-1 has a role in the pathophysiology of hypertension, and it is a potent mediator of vascular injury in hypertensive disease.

endothelin-1 (et-1) plays a role in the development and progression of hypertensive vascular injury in the rat, that the role is similar to that of angiotensin ii (ang ii), and that both vasoactive peptides are involved in the pathogenesis.

The main takeaway from our work is that
ET-1 may have an important role in the development of hypertensive vascular damage.
the vascular lesions induced by ET-1 are less severe than those produced by ANG II, and that the endothelium may play a protective role in the pathophysiology of ET-1-induced vascular lesions.
endothelin-1 is a more potent vasoconstrictor than angiotensin, and endothelin-1 causes more severe vascular lesions than does angiotensin in vivo in rats.
